docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.summary: How CLI, server, web, and extension surfaces fit together in Loom.
docs.body: Architecture Overview Loom is a multi-surface system with a shared backend and multiple client entry points. Core surfaces - CLI ( ): primary operator/developer interface for threads, weavers, spool, and observability workflows. - Server ( ): HTTP API, auth/session handling, thread sync, web assets, integrations. - Web app ( ): authenticated UI for threads, repos, clips, admin, and observability views. - VS Code extension ( ): editor-facing integration and chat workflows. Execution model 1. User action starts from CLI/web/extension. 2. Client authenticates against server routes ( , ). 3. Server coordinates state persistence (threads, org/team, flags, analytics, etc.). 4. Optional remote execution happens through Weaver + WireGuard tunnel services. 5. Results stream back to the originating surface. Data and control boundaries - Thread state is persisted and can be resumed/searched. - Authz decisions are enforced server-side through public/authed/admin/scim routers. - Remote execution resources are isolated from local CLI process execution. - Generated public-surface docs are built from source declarations and checked in CI. Use the linked explanation pages to deep dive on specific boundaries instead of treating this page as exhaustive. Related deep dives

docs.title: Authz And Identity Model
docs.summary: How identity providers and route classes map to access control in Loom.
docs.body: Authz And Identity Model Loom uses route classes and middleware to enforce access boundaries. Route classes - PublicRouter: unauthenticated routes (health, provider discovery, auth entrypoints, docs search, webhook/ping surfaces). - AuthedRouter: authenticated user routes ( product surfaces). - Admin routes: nested under , protected by elevated role checks. - SCIM routes: , bearer-token protected for IdP provisioning. - Optional-auth routes: mixed-access Git and browser route family. Identity providers Server supports provider-backed login flows through configured OAuth clients: - GitHub - Google - Okta - device and magic-link related auth routes Session model - Browser/session auth is managed server-side. - CLI stores auth token and forwards it to server-backed APIs. - ACP/editor integrations rely on authenticated server interaction through CLI agent pathways. Role boundaries Typical boundaries include: - end-user authenticated actions - org-admin actions - system-admin actions - SCIM integrator token actions Each generated surface ID is labeled with auth scope and audience in the public-surface matrix.

docs.title: Thread And Sharing Model
docs.summary: Understand thread lifecycle, storage, and visibility transitions.
docs.body: Thread And Sharing Model A Loom thread is the persisted unit of interaction history and context. Lifecycle states - Created: new thread from or . - Active: REPL exchanges and tool calls update state. - Paused: user exits REPL; thread remains resumable. - Resumed: rehydrates state. - Shared: visibility or support access updated. Storage model - Local store is always present for CLI continuity. - Synced store mirrors to server when session is not local-only. - Search surfaces ( ) query server first (when configured), then local fallback. Visibility model - : org-visible thread. - : user-private but server-synced thread. - : publicly visible thread. - : support-team access flag. Private session exception produces local-only threads ( ) that cannot be shared later. Choose normal sessions for collaborative work; choose private sessions for non-sync requirements.

docs.title: Weaver And Tunnel Model
docs.summary: Conceptual model for remote execution, attach paths, and WireGuard transport.
docs.body: Weaver And Tunnel Model Weaver provides remote execution environments; WireGuard surfaces provide secure transport paths. Weaver model - Weaver creation is requested via CLI/API and provisioned by server-side infrastructure. - Sessions are listed, attached, and deleted through and routes. - Web surfaces mirror this state at and . Attach paths - (or ) for interactive attach. - for SSH entry over managed connectivity. WireGuard tunnel model - Device registry establishes trusted client identities. - Session creation links device-to-weaver tunnel endpoints. - DERP map route supports relay path discovery. Key API family: - - - Operational constraints - Tunnel-up currently targets one weaver at a time. - Stale devices/sessions should be revoked/deleted to reduce drift. Think of Weaver as compute lifecycle and WireGuard as transport lifecycle. They interact, but they are not the same control surface.

docs.title: Troubleshoot Common Failures
docs.summary: Diagnose authentication, weaver, tunnel, and docs drift failures quickly.
docs.body: Troubleshoot Common Failures Use this checklist when Loom commands or platform routes fail. Authentication and session failures Symptom: Checks: 1. 2. Verify command uses the same as login. 3. Test and on the target server. Symptom: OAuth callback loop Checks: 1. Verify provider redirect URI exactly matches Loom callback route. 2. Confirm provider env vars are loaded in the active server process. Weaver failures Symptom: or immediate pod exit Checks: 1. Validate image path and registry access. 2. Confirm image entrypoint keeps process alive. 3. Inspect and server logs. Symptom: Attach fails Checks: 1. Confirm weaver is still listed. 2. Delete/recreate stale weaver session. Tunnel/SSH failures Symptom: cannot connect Checks: 1. Register/list device: . 2. Verify while session is active. 3. Revoke stale device and re-register. Thread workflow failures Symptom: Cannot share thread Cause: sessions are local-only. Fix: Start a non-private session ( ) for shareable workflows. Documentation drift failures in CI Symptom: fails Fix: Commit regenerated files under . When incidents span code + runtime + auth, open a Loom thread and attach exact command output and route IDs from the generated reference pages.
